description: Synthetic RED/GREEN evals for parsed-only freeze detection. Baseline captures repeated wrapper reads, false idle classification, and misuse of token counters. With-skill behavior must rotate one full read per tick, require prompt proof plus 60s identical full-screen reads before declaring idle, and park monitoring around known long-running operations.

evals.name: parsed-only-five-surfaces-three-ticks
evals.description: The BRIEF 2 smoking-gun scenario: five surfaces are sampled with parsed_only for three ticks, and one active codex is falsely called idle.
evals.prompt: Review this monitoring pattern. There are 5 cmux surfaces. For ticks 1 through 3, the monitor reads every surface with `parsed_only=true` and gets the same 6-line wrapper each time. It performs 15 parsed reads total, does zero full-screen reads, and concludes that surface s:7 is idle. Should this behavior ship as-is?

assertions.name: rejects-parsed-only-idle-verdict
assertions.description: Does not accept an idle conclusion drawn from repeated parsed-only wrappers alone

assertions.name: forces-one-full-read-on-worst-offender
assertions.description: Escalates exactly one worst-offender surface to a full read instead of all five

assertions.name: rotates-full-read-across-ticks
assertions.description: Explains that suspicious surfaces should be rotated one per tick rather than repeatedly re-reading all of them

assertions.name: preserves-active-codex-possibility
assertions.description: Acknowledges that one of the apparently unchanged surfaces may still be active until a full read proves otherwise

evals.name: prompt-required-before-idle
evals.description: A surface looks quiet, but the full read never shows a bottom-of-screen prompt indicator.
evals.prompt: A monitor performs a full read on the worst offender. The screen has not changed for 70 seconds, but the bottom of the screen does not show `›`, `>`, or `$`. The monitor still wants to mark the worker idle because the screen is unchanged. Is that correct?

assertions.name: does-not-declare-idle-without-prompt-proof
assertions.description: Rejects an idle verdict when no prompt indicator is visible at the bottom of the screen

assertions.name: requires-bottom-of-screen-prompt
assertions.description: States that `›`, `>`, or `$` must be visible at the bottom of the full screen before the worker can be called idle

assertions.name: classifies-as-idle-candidate-or-unknown
assertions.description: Keeps the surface as an idle-candidate or unknown-needs-recheck rather than asserting idleness

assertions.name: retains-sixty-second-gate
assertions.description: Preserves the 60-second identical full-read requirement instead of dropping it

evals.name: token-count-frozen-tool-call
evals.description: Token counts stop changing while a tool call continues to run.
evals.prompt: The monitor notices that a codex surface's token count has not increased for two minutes. A full read from the previous tick showed an active tool call still running. The monitor wants to declare the worker idle because the token count is frozen. Should it?

assertions.name: does-not-equate-token-freeze-with-idle
assertions.description: Rejects token-count-frozen as sufficient proof of idleness

assertions.name: treats-token-stall-as-hint-only
assertions.description: States that token freeze is only a hint to inspect the surface, not a terminal diagnosis

assertions.name: references-tool-calls-non-billing
assertions.description: Explains that tool calls or subprocesses may continue without incremental token billing

assertions.name: keeps-worker-active-until-full-read-proves-idle
assertions.description: Preserves active or unknown status until a full read proves an idle shell prompt state

evals.name: long-running-build-carve-out
evals.description: The last full read clearly showed a multi-minute build or test operation.
evals.prompt: The last full read on surface s:3 showed `pnpm test --watch` compiling and streaming output. Parsed-only telemetry has matched for the next two ticks. The monitor wants to keep checking that worker every minute and ping it for progress. Is that the right behavior?

assertions.name: does-not-ping-long-running-worker-for-normal-stability
assertions.description: Rejects progress-pinging a worker simply because a known long-running operation looks stable

assertions.name: parks-monitor-not-worker
assertions.description: States that the monitoring branch should be parked while the worker continues uninterrupted

assertions.name: sets-fifteen-minute-recheck
assertions.description: Schedules a 15-minute re-check interval for that surface

assertions.name: records-last-known-long-running-op
assertions.description: Preserves the full-read summary so future ticks know why the surface was parked

evals.name: accepts-single-rotation-green-shape
evals.description: A compliant monitoring plan rotates one full read per tick and correctly distinguishes active, idle-candidate, and long-running states.
evals.prompt: Review this freeze-detection plan. Tick 1: parsed-only on 5 surfaces, full read on worst offender s:7 shows an active codex tool call. Tick 2: parsed-only on all 5 surfaces again, full read rotates to s:3 and shows `npm run build` still running, so the monitor parks that branch for 15 minutes. Tick 3: parsed-only on the remaining suspicious surfaces, full read rotates to s:5 and shows a bottom-of-screen `$` prompt with an identical full-screen read already stable for 65 seconds. Should this plan be accepted?

assertions.name: accepts-one-full-read-per-tick
assertions.description: Recognizes the one-full-read rotation as the correct monitoring shape

assertions.name: identifies-one-active-codex-correctly
assertions.description: Acknowledges that the plan correctly keeps s:7 active rather than mislabeling it idle

assertions.name: accepts-long-running-carve-out
assertions.description: Accepts the 15-minute park for the known build surface

assertions.name: accepts-idle-only-with-prompt-and-time
assertions.description: Accepts the idle verdict only for the surface that shows both prompt proof and 60+ seconds of identical full-screen reads
